annotationRationale: Incircle and circumcircle properties locate I and O. Internal tangency and coordinate distance determine M, after which shoelace computes the area.
sourceMethod: Follows the official coordinate solution with its shoelace area calculation. Expands the radius equation and justifies internal tangency using the stated leg segments.

review.mathCheck: Tangency to both leg segments forces M=(ρ,ρ), with 0<ρ≤5. Its contact on AC lies inside the circumcircle; since ρ<R, tangency must be internal. The distance equation reduces to ρ(ρ−4)=0. The positive root 4 satisfies all segment and tangency constraints. With O=(6,5/2) and I=(2,2), shoelace gives area 7/2, choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of Q21's coordinate-and-shoelace MAA solution on pages 13–14. It agrees with the supplied figure and adds valid internal-tangency justification and the omitted radius algebra.
review.annotationCheck: Incircle, circumcircle, and circle-position properties are correctly assessed. Coordinate distance, the inradius-area relation, and shoelace appropriately support locating M and computing the area.
